question: Which strains of HPV are most commonly linked to cervical cancer?
explanation: Strains 16 and 18 are high-risk types responsible for the majority of cervical cancers worldwide. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h1)

question: What usually happens to an HPV infection in the body after a year or two?

options.A: It is cleared naturally by the immune system
options.B: It lies dormant forever without any cellular changes
options.C: It transforms permanently into benign genital warts
options.D: It immediately develops into invasive cervical cancer

explanation: A healthy immune system typically fights off and clears most HPV infections without causing lasting harm. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h1)

question: Who is the primary target group recommended to receive the HPV vaccine?
explanation: Vaccinating young adolescent girls before sexual debut provides maximum protection before potential exposure to the virus. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why is the HPV vaccine considered a form of primary prevention?

options.A: It treats active genital warts caused by low-risk viral strains
options.B: It prevents the initial acquisition of the virus before infection occurs
options.C: It cures existing cervical cancer cells within a few weeks of treatment
options.D: It replaces the need for any future routine cervical cancer screening

explanation: Primary prevention stops a condition from happening in the first place by building immunity against the virus. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which screening method is most widely used and practical for primary health care settings in Nigeria?
explanation: VIA is affordable, needs minimal equipment, and gives immediate results, making it ideal for primary clinics. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of a 'screen-and-treat' VIA protocol in remote rural communities?

options.A: It guarantees that she will never contract a viral infection again
options.B: It prevents patient loss to follow-up by treating immediately
options.C: It proves definitively that she already has invasive malignant cancer
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any physical pelvic examination

explanation: Many women in rural areas find it hard to return for follow-up visits, so treating precancerous changes during the same visit saves lives. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which part of the cervix must be sampled during a Pap smear to get an adequate cell specimen?
explanation: The transformation zone is where most cervical changes start, making it the key target for cell collection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h4)

question: What does an LSIL result typically mean on a lab report?

options.A: Large spreading invasive malignant tumor of the uterus
options.B: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion with mild dysplasia
options.C: Complete absence of any epithelial cells on the slide
options.D: Normal tissue with zero inflammation or cellular changes

explanation: LSIL stands for low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, which shows mild, often temporary cell changes from HPV. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h4)

question: What color do abnormal precancerous cells turn when exposed to acetic acid during a VIA exam?
explanation: Acetic acid causes proteins in abnormal cells to turn a noticeable whitish color against the pink cervix. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of using VIA for cervical cancer screening?

options.A: It is subjective and depends heavily on the provider's visual judgment
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory machinery to analyze the tissue samples
options.C: It causes permanent chemical burns on the healthy parts of the cervix
options.D: It takes at least two weeks for the vinegar reaction results to appear

explanation: Because VIA relies on the naked eye rather than automated lab tests, the provider's skill level affects its accuracy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why is pre-test counseling important before performing a cervical screening test?

options.A: It guarantees that the client will never test positive for an infection
options.B: It chemically alters the cervical cells to make them easier to stain
options.C: It reduces patient anxiety and addresses misconceptions about the procedure
options.D: It completely replaces the need to perform a physical pelvic exam

explanation: Good counseling prepares the client emotionally, explains what to expect, and encourages participation in screening. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h6)

question: A client has a screening result showing a suspicious, advanced cervical lesion. What is the most appropriate next step for the midwife?

options.A: Reassure her that no medical follow-up is ever needed for abnormal results
options.B: Discharge the client and advise her to return in five years for a repeat test
options.C: Administer a dose of routine childhood HPV vaccine to cure the lesion
options.D: Refer the client urgently to a gynecologist for colposcopy and biopsy

explanation: Suspicious or advanced lesions need immediate specialist evaluation and tissue testing to confirm diagnosis and plan care. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h6)
